proof:
Source: step 1 of the selected proof of cmcdtfrbv_boundary_support_subset_faces (Z := ⋃_{q∈s} Φ_q(Cⁿ) is compact).

Notation. C := {y ∈ Euclid (m+1) : 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 for every i} is the closed unit cube.

1. C is closed. By set extensionality, C = ⋂_i ({y : 0 ≤ y_i} ∩ {y : y_i ≤ 1}). Each coordinate map y ↦ y_i on Euclid (m+1) is continuous (fun_prop). Comparing it with a constant, {y : 0 ≤ y_i} and {y : y_i ≤ 1} are closed (isClosed_le with continuous_const). Their intersection is closed (IsClosed.inter), and so is the intersection over all i (isClosed_iInter).
2. C is bounded. Let y ∈ C. For every i, 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 gives |y_i|² = y_i·y_i ≤ 1·1 = 1. Hence ‖y‖ = √(Σ_i |y_i|²) (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq) ≤ √(Σ_i 1) = √(m+1) (Finset.sum_le_sum and Real.sqrt_le_sqrt). So C ⊆ closedBall(0, √(m+1)), and C is bounded (Metric.isBounded_iff_subset_closedBall).
3. C is compact. Euclid (m+1) is a finite-dimensional real normed space, hence a proper metric space, and a closed bounded subset of a proper space is compact (Metric.isCompact_of_isClosed_isBounded, applied to steps 1 and 2).
4. Each Φ_q(C) is compact. Φ_q(y) = b + Σ_j y_j • e_{ι(j)} is a constant vector plus a finite sum of the maps y ↦ y_j • e_{ι(j)}. Each of these is a continuous coordinate times a constant vector. Constants, finite sums and scalar multiples of continuous maps are continuous (fun_prop), so Φ_q is continuous. The continuous image of a compact set is compact (IsCompact.image), so Φ_q(C) is compact.
5. Z = ⋃_{q∈s} Φ_q(C). By definition, x ∈ Z iff there are q ∈ s and y ∈ C with Φ_q(y) = x. That holds iff x ∈ Φ_q(C) for some q ∈ s (set extensionality with mem_iUnion and mem_image).
6. A union of compact sets indexed by the finite set s is compact (Finset.isCompact_biUnion). By steps 4 and 5, Z is compact. ∎
key_steps: The closed unit cube C ⊆ Euclid (m+1) is closed, as an intersection of coordinate half-spaces, and bounded, since ‖y‖ ≤ √(m+1). Hence it is compact.
Each affine map Φ_q is continuous, so Φ_q(C) is compact.
Z = ⋃_{q∈s} Φ_q(C) is a finite union of compact sets, hence compact.
